note: Window agent p1770-p1779, 2 Nov 2026. Six pages opened: Quebec Act, Province of Quebec (1763-1791), Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata, First Partition of Poland, Louisiana (New Spain), Province of Massachusetts Bay.

region.text: the western parts of the Vitebsk and Mogilev lands (Braslaw, Glubokoye, Lepel, Bobruisk side), i.e. the part of those two oblasts outside Cliopatria's Russian shape of 1772, which lay west of the Dvina-Drut-Dnieper line

events.note: 1772 (First Partition): Russia received 'the commonwealth territories east of the line formed roughly by the Dvina, Drut, and Dnieper rivers' (the counties of Vitebsk, Polotsk and Mstislavl, and Livonia). The russian-empire gain of 22 September names the whole of Vitebsk and Mogilev, but the Russian keyframe of 1772 holds only the part east of that line, so the snap released the rest to nobody (132 cells, 1772-1774) until Poland's 1775 keyframe took it back. The rest stays Polish.

region.text: Minnesota east of the Mississippi (the east bank from Winona and Red Wing up past St. Cloud and Brainerd to the Arrowhead); the polygon is my reading of the river's course, coarse at cell scale

events.note: The 1763 Treaty of Paris split Upper Louisiana 'at the Mississippi River' with 'the west going to Spain'; Spanish Louisiana 'encompassed the entire Mississippi Basin to the west, starting from the right bank of the Mississippi River'. The gazetteer's Louisiana region still holds the Minnesota east bank (the dossier's note says so), so the cells go to nobody from the start of the window; the Quebec Act keyframe takes them in 1774.

region.text: the District of Maine, part of the Province of Massachusetts Bay

events.note: The Massachusetts Bay charter of 1692 'included the Massachusetts Bay Colony, the Plymouth Colony, the Province of Maine, the Territory of Sagadahock', and 'Maine was not separated until after American independence, when it attained statehood in 1820'. The dossier draws the colonies from modern state names, which leaves Maine out; the British Colonial Empire's shape held it directly until its 1775 keyframe dropped it, leaving it unowned for 1775.

intersect.text: roughly today's Argentina, northern Chile, Bolivia, Paraguay and Uruguay

union.text: the Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata, 'roughly today's Argentina, northern Chile, Bolivia, Paraguay and Uruguay', as far as Spain held it
the Governorate of Chucuito (Puno), a governorate of the viceroyalty from 1776
the Misiones Orientales, the seven missions east of the Uruguay, part of the Government of the Misiones Guaranies

correction.text: the Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata as far as Spain held it, with Chucuito (Puno) and the Misiones Orientales, both inside the viceroyalty until 1796 and 1801

keyframe_overrides.why: The page lists 'Governorate of Chucuito (1776-1784)' and 'Political and Military Government of the Misiones Guaraníes (1776-1810)' among the governorates, says 'The Intendancy of Puno became part of the Viceroyalty of Peru in 1796' and that the Misiones Orientales, 'part of the Political and Military Government of the Misiones Guaraníes', were captured by Portugal in 1801-1802. The dossier's own ledger has the 1796 and 1801 losses, but its keyframe (countries only) left Puno and the Misiones out, so the snap of 1776 gave 263 Puno cells and about 226 Misiones cells to the Spanish Empire direct and the later losses had nothing to remove.

keyframe_overrides.why: The shape adds the gazetteer's whole Louisiana region, which still holds Minnesota east of the river (the spanish-louisiana note says so); the Louisiana (New Spain) page has the Mississippi River split Upper Louisiana in 1763 'with the west going to Spain' and Spanish Louisiana beginning 'from the right bank'. Without the cut the umbrella took 118 east-bank cells in 1772-1773 after events/1 had freed them; the Quebec Act keyframe takes them in 1774. The rest of the shape is unchanged.

region.text: Minnesota west of the Mississippi (my reading of the river's course)

rulings.why: The Quebec Act of 1774 extended Quebec 'west to the Mississippi River', and Spanish Louisiana began 'from the right bank of the Mississippi River' (Louisiana (New Spain) page). The Quebec keyframe draws all of Minnesota, so the cells west of the river (about 87 of the 194 both claim, south-east and central Minnesota) stay Spanish; the east bank is Quebec's.

The Province of Quebec was its own British colony, 'established by the Kingdom of Great Britain in 1763' and enlarged by the Quebec Act of 1774; the British Colonial Empire is Cliopatria's umbrella shape. The size rule (R1) gave the umbrella 453 cells of Quebec's own St Lawrence land in 1775 (its Cliopatria area was the smaller), the 1776 keyframe of the umbrella then released 178 of them to nobody, and 1778 took them back; the colony keeps its land throughout.

The Quebec Act extended Quebec 'north to the southern boundary of lands owned by the Hudson's Bay Company, or Rupert's Land'; the Quebec keyframe of 1774 overlaps the Rupert's Land keyframe (the Hudson Bay drainage as that dossier draws it) in 468 cells, 202 in northern Minnesota north of 47 N and 266 in the 49-50 N band of north-western Ontario, all held by Rupert's Land before 1774, so Rupert's Land keeps them. [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: cell figures corrected from the trial; the why had named 266 cells of north-western Minnesota.]
